193.closing_lemma: A weighted abelian-square lemma for arbitrary finite rank-three step sets with infinite prefix-sum range.
193.minimal_test: Exhaust all ternary words through length 8 and combine the threshold with a rank split.
rigorous_findings: Every ternary length-8 word contains an abelian square; the survivor counts by lengths 1..8 are 3,6,12,18,30,30,18,0.
The size-at-most-three step-set case follows after separating rank at most two from rank three.
This subcase is already Gerver--Ramsey (1979), Theorem 3, and is not a new result.
193.first_breakpoint: Four letters: ordinary Parikh equality is avoidable, while a rank-three weighted map has a nontrivial kernel and arbitrary-ratio collinearity remains.
193.publication_assessment: No new theorem; explicitly present in the 1979 primary source.

91.public_claim_status: A May 2026 official-forum comment claims and sketches a density-one partial theorem; this intake independently verified it.
91.closing_lemma: Prove non-uniqueness for the terminal sizes M(k), M(k)-1, and M(k)-2 of every sufficiently large attained distance plateau.
91.minimal_test: Independently verify the May 2026 density-one counting proof, its N=15 threshold, and the logical sufficiency of bounded-gap plateaux.
rigorous_findings: The public density-one proof is valid: all but at most three sizes per plateau have two non-similar minimizers.
The exceptional set up to N has size at most 3f(N)+O(1)=o(N).
Bounded-gap plateaux do not imply deletion preserves f(n), and sublinearity alone permits arbitrarily long strict-increase runs.
91.first_breakpoint: The last three sizes of each plateau, not the distance between successive plateaux.
91.publication_assessment: The density-one theorem is an existing public comment, not a new output of this intake; the route audit is not paper-level.

509.public_claim_status: A May 2026 official-forum attachment proposes a stronger partition claim but explicitly leaves its main quantitative bound unproved.
509.closing_lemma: First prove total-radius-two coverage for every disconnected cubic whose root minimum-enclosing radius exceeds one; the all-degree problem still needs a component-partition inequality.
509.minimal_test: Compare cubic root triples with identical MST edge lengths using the exact critical-value connectedness criterion.
rigorous_findings: Root minimum-enclosing radius at most one gives a one-disc radius-two cover in every degree.
A cubic with a root pair at distance at most 0.220236850315... has an explicit two-disc cover of total radius two.
Equilateral and collinear triples with MST lengths {3/2,3/2} have critical-value moduli 3sqrt(3)/8 and 3sqrt(3)/4, hence opposite connectedness.
509.first_breakpoint: The two MST lengths omit the included angle/third edge and therefore do not determine critical values or lemniscate topology.
509.publication_assessment: Only elementary sufficient regimes and a route counterexample; no cubic closure or improved universal constant.

1002.closing_lemma: A uniform weak-L1 tail gives tightness; a second uniqueness/characteristic-function lemma is still required for the original all-c distributional limit.
1002.minimal_test: Exact Farey-cell integration at n=64,128,256, including tails, absolute first moments, and an independent gcd covariance identity.
rigorous_findings: S_n is affine with common slope -n(n+1)/2 on Farey cells and jumps by floor(n/q) at reduced p/q.
The exact second moment is (1/12) sum gcd(k,l)^2/(kl), at least n/12, so uniform L2 tightness is impossible.
Finite exact tail data are compatible with C/A, but do not prove it.
Naive absolute Denjoy--Koksma/Ostrowski summation has a typical extra log log n loss.
1002.first_breakpoint: Cancellation among heavy Ostrowski digits of size about log n; neither second moments nor absolute block bounds reach the desired scale.
1002.publication_assessment: No new asymptotic estimate or limit theorem; exact diagnostics are research infrastructure only.

claim_guard: All four original Erdős problems remain open. No finite certificate, public comment, known theorem, or topology counterpair is represented as closure.
